chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from someone else from Aban from a man from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:
Regarding the man who dies with the people in the sea, he said: He is washed, and enshrouded, and Salat is prayed over him, and weighted, and thrown into the sea.

key_terms.يُثْقَلُ: He is weighted (with stones or lead to sink)
key_terms.يُصَلَّى عَلَيْهِ: Prayer is prayed over him (funeral prayer)
key_terms.يُغَسَّلُ: He is washed (ritual bath for the dead)
key_terms.يُكَفَّنُ: He is enshrouded (wrapped in burial cloth)

ai.seo_question: What are the funeral rites for a Muslim who dies at sea?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a practical legal ruling for maritime deaths where retrieving the body is impractical. It confirms that the deceased retains full ritual status, undergoing complete *ghusl*, *kafan*, and *Salat al-Janazah* before being weighted and committed to the sea, reflecting the Shia emphasis on preserving the dignity of the deceased even in unique environmental conditions.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad, from someone else, from Aban, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

having said regarding the man who dies with the group in the sea, so heasws said: ‘He should be washed, and enshrouded, and Salaat would be prayed over him, and weight (tied to him), and he would be thrown into the sea’.
en.sarwar: 2. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad from more than one person from Aban from a man who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

was asked about one who dies in the company of people in the ocean. He (the Imam) said, ‘Ghusl (bath), shroud and Salah (prayer) are done for him and with some weight tied to him is thrown in the ocean.’”
